I would keep to the wheat-maize rotation that fits Quzhou County best, because it matches the local climate, my irrigation conditions, and the way I would manage risk at my age. At 68, I would not spread myself across too many different crops. I would rather run a simple, disciplined system on land I can manage well than chase higher upside with more labor and market uncertainty. Since it is the start of the growing season, I would carry the winter wheat already in the ground through harvest, then I would plant summer maize right after. With a high education level, I would lean on improved or hybrid seed, measured fertilizer use, and fewer but more targeted field operations. I would use ploughing before wheat where residue or compaction is a problem, then rotary tillage for the maize after wheat harvest so I can turn the crop quickly. I would irrigate wheat more often because its spring water demand is more sensitive here, and I would keep maize irrigation moderate unless rainfall is clearly short. I would not overapply nitrogen, because that raises lodging and waste; I would keep phosphorus and potassium in balance to protect yield stability. I would also keep pesticide sprays limited and timed to actual disease, weed, and insect pressure rather than spraying blindly.
